questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question_text: Phenylketonuria (PKU): enzyme deficient?
questions.explanation: PKU: phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency → phenylalanine accumulates → phenylpyruvate in urine (musty odor), intellectual disability, fair complexion. Diet: restrict phenylalanine.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question_text: JVP: which component corresponds to atrial contraction?
questions.explanation: JVP waves: a=atrial contraction, c=tricuspid valve closure (small), v=venous filling during ventricular systole, x=atrial relaxation, y=tricuspid opens. Absent a wave: AF. Giant a: pulmonary hypertension.

questions.subject: Ophthalmology
questions.question_text: Argyll Robertson pupil: characteristics?

options.B: Does not react to light but reacts to accommodation (near)

questions.explanation: Argyll Robertson pupil: accommodation-convergence reflex intact, but light reflex ABSENT (midbrain dorsal lesion). Classic in neurosyphilis. Bilateral, irregular, small (miotic) pupils.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.question_text: Most common cyanotic congenital heart disease at birth?
questions.explanation: Most common cyanotic CHD at BIRTH: TGA (complete). Most common cyanotic CHD overall in childhood: TOF. TGA: parallel circuits, needs mixing (ASD/VSD/PDA). Prostaglandin E1 to keep PDA open.

questions.subject: Forensic Medicine
questions.question_text: Putrefaction: first sign?

options.B: Greenish discoloration of right iliac fossa (cecum area)

questions.explanation: Putrefaction: first sign is greenish discoloration of right iliac fossa (cecal bacteria: H2S + Hb → green sulfhemoglobin). Then marbling, bloating, skin slippage. Rate influenced by temperature and environment.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.question_text: Neonatal jaundice: physiological jaundice appears?
questions.explanation: Physiological jaundice: appears after 24 hours (day 2-3), peaks day 4-5, resolves by day 14 in term (21 in preterm). Pathological: appears <24h, bilirubin rising >5mg/dL/day, >12 mg/dL in term.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) grade III?

options.B: Reflux to renal pelvis, no dilatation
options.D: Moderate dilatation with loss of fornices

questions.explanation: VUR grades: I=ureter only, II=pelvis+calyces no dilation, III=mild dilation, IV=moderate dilation loss of fornices, V=severe with tortuous ureter.

questions.subject: PSM
questions.question_text: Infant mortality rate (IMR) formula?
questions.explanation: IMR = deaths in <1 year / live births in same year × 1000. Sensitive indicator of socioeconomic development. Includes neonatal (<28 days) and post-neonatal (28 days-1 year).

questions.subject: OBGYN
questions.question_text: Magnesium sulfate in eclampsia: first sign of toxicity?
questions.explanation: MgSO4 toxicity sequence: loss of DTRs (8-10 mg/dL) → respiratory paralysis (12-15) → cardiac arrest (>15). Monitor: RR >12/min, UO >25 mL/hr, patellar reflexes present. Antidote: calcium gluconate.

questions.subject: Forensic Medicine
questions.question_text: Rape examination: must be done by?

options.B: Any registered medical practitioner (male or female)

questions.explanation: Rape examination (as per BNS/BNSS replacing IPC/CrPC): to be conducted by any registered medical practitioner. Consent of survivor is mandatory. Report to be sent to police. Evidence: DNA, swabs, injuries.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Type of drain used after thyroid surgery?
questions.explanation: Closed suction drains (Redivac/Jackson-Pratt) are used after thyroid/neck surgery to prevent hematoma. Corrugated and Penrose are open drains.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question_text: Vitamin K: mechanism of action?

options.B: Cofactor for gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors II, VII, IX, X

questions.explanation: Vitamin K: required for gamma-carboxylation (activation) of clotting factors II, VII, IX, X and proteins C/S. Warfarin blocks vitamin K epoxide reductase. Deficiency: prolonged PT.

questions.subject: Ophthalmology
questions.question_text: Primary open-angle glaucoma: optic disc finding?
questions.explanation: POAG: progressive optic neuropathy. CDR >0.5 or asymmetry >0.2 is significant. Superotemporal and inferotemporal RNFL loss first → arcuate scotomas. Gradual, painless, peripheral vision loss.

questions.subject: ENT
questions.question_text: Most common cause of hoarseness in adults?
questions.explanation: Most common cause of hoarseness: acute laryngitis (viral). Chronic hoarseness >3 weeks: evaluate for laryngeal Ca. Vocal cord nodules: singers/voice misuse. Unilateral vocal cord palsy: consider lung/mediastinal pathology.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.question_text: CMV inclusion in salivary gland disease?
questions.explanation: CMV: 'owl-eye' large intranuclear inclusions with surrounding halo. Also cytoplasmic inclusions. Causes congenital infection (periventricular calcifications), retinitis in HIV.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Most common thyroid cancer?
questions.explanation: Papillary thyroid Ca: most common (80%), best prognosis, psammoma bodies, Orphan Annie nuclei, lymphatic spread. Associated with radiation exposure.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Gottron's papules and heliotrope rash are features of?
questions.explanation: Dermatomyositis: Gottron's papules (over knuckles), heliotrope rash (periorbital), shawl sign, V-sign. Anti-Mi-2 antibody.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.question_text: Developmental milestone: walking alone at?
questions.explanation: Gross motor milestones: lifts head 1m, sits unsupported 6-7m, stands with support 8m, walks with support 10-11m, walks alone 12-15m. Red flag: not walking by 18 months.

questions.subject: Ophthalmology
questions.question_text: Diabetic retinopathy: first sign?
questions.explanation: DR progression: microaneurysms (earliest) → dot/blot hemorrhages → hard exudates → cotton wool spots (NPDR) → neovascularization (PDR). FFA: leakage from microaneurysms.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Indication for calcium supplementation after thyroidectomy?
questions.explanation: Hypoparathyroidism after thyroidectomy (PTH fall, low Ca): treat with calcium + calcitriol. Monitor Ca at 24-48h. Permanent hypoparathyroidism needs lifelong supplementation.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Killip class III in acute MI indicates?
questions.explanation: Killip classification: I=no failure, II=S3 + basal crackles, III=frank pulmonary edema, IV=cardiogenic shock. Mortality increases with class.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Courvoisier's law states?

options.A: In jaundice with palpable GB, cause is unlikely to be gallstones
options.B: In jaundice with palpable GB, cause is likely to be gallstones
options.D: GB is never palpable in hepatitis

questions.explanation: Courvoisier's law: painless jaundice + palpable GB = unlikely gallstones (GB fibrosed in chronic stone disease). Suggests malignancy (pancreatic Ca, cholangiocarcinoma).

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Virchow's triad for DVT includes all EXCEPT?
questions.explanation: Virchow's triad: stasis + endothelial injury + hypercoagulability. Arterial spasm is not part of it (relevant to Raynaud's/arterial disease).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question_text: Mesonephric (Wolffian) duct in females gives rise to?

options.B: Bartholin's glands (vestibular glands) — vestigial Gartner's duct cysts

questions.explanation: In females, Wolffian duct regresses (vestigial) → Gartner's duct cysts (vaginal). Müllerian (paramesonephric) ducts → fallopian tubes, uterus, upper vagina. Ovaries from genital ridge.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.question_text: Drug with zero-order kinetics at therapeutic doses?
questions.explanation: Phenytoin exhibits zero-order kinetics at therapeutic doses (saturated enzyme system). Small dose increase → disproportionate rise in plasma levels → toxicity.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.question_text: PAN (Polyarteritis Nodosa): vessels involved?
questions.explanation: PAN: medium-vessel vasculitis, spares lungs. Segmental fibrinoid necrosis. p-ANCA usually negative. Hepatitis B association. Causes mononeuritis multiplex.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.question_text: Minimum alveolar concentration (MAC): definition?

options.B: Alveolar concentration preventing movement in response to surgical stimulus in 50% of patients

questions.explanation: MAC: minimum alveolar concentration at 1 ATM at which 50% of patients don't move to surgical incision. Desflurane MAC=6%, Sevoflurane=2%, Isoflurane=1.15%. Decreased by: old age, hypothermia, opioids.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.question_text: FDA Pregnancy category X drug?
questions.explanation: Category X (absolute contraindication in pregnancy): thalidomide, isotretinoin, methotrexate, statins, warfarin (1st trimester teratogenic → category X). Note: FDA removed letter system in 2015 but USMLE/NEET use it.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.question_text: Dopamine pathway involved in Parkinson's disease?
questions.explanation: Parkinson's: loss of dopaminergic neurons in substantia nigra → reduced nigrostriatal dopamine → basal ganglia imbalance → tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.question_text: Drug causing red man syndrome?
questions.explanation: Red man syndrome (vancomycin): histamine release during rapid infusion → flushing, erythema, urticaria of neck/face. NOT allergy — prevented by slow infusion.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.question_text: Marker for Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH)?
questions.explanation: LCH: Birbeck granules (tennis racket shape on EM), CD1a+, Langerin (CD207)+, S100+. Involves bone, skin, lung, pituitary (DI).

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.question_text: Disulfiram mechanism in alcohol dependence?

options.B: Inhibits aldehyde dehydrogenase → acetaldehyde accumulation (flushing, nausea)

questions.explanation: Disulfiram: aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibitor. Alcohol → acetaldehyde (normally → acetic acid). Disulfiram blocks ALDH → acetaldehyde accumulates → flushing, tachycardia, vomiting. Aversion therapy.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.question_text: Reed-Sternberg cells are pathognomonic of?
questions.explanation: Reed-Sternberg cells: large binucleated 'owl-eye' cells (CD15+, CD30+, CD45-). Classic in nodular sclerosis Hodgkin's lymphoma (most common subtype).

questions.subject: PSM
questions.question_text: Sensitivity of 80% and specificity of 90% for disease prevalence 10%. PPV is?
questions.explanation: PPV = TP/(TP+FP). With prev 10%: TP=80, FP=90 (10% of 900 = 90), PPV = 80/(80+90) = 47%. PPV increases with higher prevalence. This shows PPV is context-dependent.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question_text: Persistent truncus arteriosus results from failure of?
questions.explanation: Persistent truncus arteriosus: failure of aorticopulmonary septum to form → single vessel from both ventricles. DiGeorge syndrome (22q11.2 deletion) association.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question_text: Gaucher disease: enzyme deficient?
questions.explanation: Gaucher disease: most common lysosomal storage disease. Glucocerebrosidase deficiency → glucocerebroside accumulation. Gaucher cells (wrinkled tissue paper appearance) in liver/spleen/bone marrow.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.question_text: Weil-Felix test is positive in?
questions.explanation: Weil-Felix: cross-reaction between Rickettsia and Proteus OX antigens (OX-2, OX-19, OX-K). Used as surrogate test for rickettsial infections.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.question_text: Tzanck smear is positive in?

options.B: HSV and VZV (acantholytic cells/multinucleate giant cells)

questions.explanation: Tzanck smear: scraping from base of vesicle → multinucleated giant cells/acantholytic cells in HSV and VZV (chickenpox). Also positive in pemphigus vulgaris (acantholytic cells, no giant cells).

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.question_text: Most radiosensitive cells?
questions.explanation: Bergonié-Tribondeau law: cells most radiosensitive are undifferentiated, rapidly dividing, with high mitotic activity. Most sensitive: lymphocytes, gonads, bone marrow. Least: neurons, muscle.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Medullary thyroid carcinoma is associated with?
questions.explanation: MTC: RET mutation (MEN2A, MEN2B, familial MTC). Secretes calcitonin. Amyloid stroma. Most aggressive hereditary variant: MEN2B with marfanoid habitus.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Whipple's disease organism?
questions.explanation: Whipple's disease: T. whipplei (actinomycete). PAS-positive macrophages in small bowel. Triad: malabsorption, arthralgia, fever.

questions.subject: OBGYN
questions.question_text: FIGO staging of cervical cancer: stage IIB?
questions.explanation: FIGO cervical Ca: I=cervix only, IIA=upper vagina no parametrium, IIB=parametrial involvement, IIIA=lower 1/3 vagina, IIIB=pelvic wall/hydronephrosis, IVA=bladder/rectum, IVB=distant mets.

questions.subject: Orthopedics
questions.question_text: Posterior dislocation of hip: position of limb?
questions.explanation: Posterior hip dislocation (most common, 90%): limb held ADDUCTED, INTERNALLY ROTATED, SHORTENED, slightly flexed. Complication: sciatic nerve injury (most common), AVN of femoral head.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.question_text: Fibrinoid necrosis is characteristic of?
questions.explanation: Fibrinoid necrosis: eosinophilic amorphous deposits in vessel walls. Seen in malignant hypertension, immune complex vasculitis (SLE, PAN), rheumatic fever.

questions.subject: ENT
questions.question_text: Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma (JNA): characteristics?

options.B: Benign hypervascular tumor in adolescent boys, arising from sphenopalatine foramen

questions.explanation: JNA: benign but locally aggressive, highly vascular. Adolescent males only. Arises from sphenopalatine foramen. Presents with recurrent unilateral epistaxis. Diagnosis: CT (do NOT biopsy).

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.question_text: Enzyme inducer that also induces its own metabolism (autoinduction)?
questions.explanation: Carbamazepine: autoinduction — induces CYP3A4 including its own metabolism. Initial dose needs increase after 3-4 weeks. Rifampicin also induces but less 'auto'.

questions.subject: ENT
questions.question_text: Most common site of epistaxis?
questions.explanation: Little's area/Kiesselbach's plexus: anterior inferior nasal septum — confluence of 4 arteries (branches of anterior ethmoidal, sphenopalatine, superior labial, greater palatine). 90% of nosebleeds.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Contraindication to thrombolysis in acute ischemic stroke?
questions.explanation: Absolute CI to tPA: recent major surgery <14 days, hemorrhage, BP >185/110 (uncontrolled), INR >1.7. Age >80 is NOT absolute CI.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Thyroglossal cyst: most common site?
questions.explanation: Thyroglossal cyst: most common at or below hyoid bone (subhyoid). Moves with tongue protrusion and swallowing. Sistrunk operation.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.question_text: Suxamethonium (succinylcholine) mechanism?

options.B: Depolarizing NM blocker (mimics ACh at NMJ continuously)

questions.explanation: Succinylcholine: depolarizing NMB — persistently activates NMJ → phase I (depolarizing) block → fasciculations then flaccid paralysis. Fastest onset (60s), shortest duration (10min). Triggers malignant hyperthermia.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.question_text: Giant cell tumor of bone: most common site?
questions.explanation: GCT: EPIPHYSIS of long bones (distal femur, proximal tibia most common). Eccentric, lytic, 'soap bubble' appearance. Multinucleated giant cells.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Drug of choice for rate control in AF with heart failure (EF<40%)?
questions.explanation: Beta-blockers (carvedilol/metoprolol) are preferred in AF with HFrEF. Digoxin can be added but not first-line alone.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question_text: Which nerve is damaged in 'Saturday night palsy'?
questions.explanation: Saturday night palsy: radial nerve compression in spiral groove of humerus → wrist drop, loss of finger extension. Sensory loss on dorsal hand. Triceps spared (injury below its branch).

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.question_text: OCD: ego-dystonic or ego-syntonic?
questions.explanation: OCD: obsessions are ego-DYSTONIC — patient recognizes thoughts as own but unwanted/distressing. Unlike delusions (ego-syntonic). Insight present (unlike psychosis). Treat with SSRI + CBT/ERP.

questions.subject: PSM
questions.question_text: Relative risk of 1.0 means?

options.A: Disease twice as common in exposed
options.B: No association between exposure and disease
options.C: Disease half as common in exposed

questions.explanation: RR=1: no association. RR>1: risk factor. RR<1: protective. RR calculated from cohort studies. OR from case-control studies (approximates RR when disease rare).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question_text: Nerve injured in anterior dislocation of shoulder?
questions.explanation: Anterior shoulder dislocation: most common dislocation. Complications: axillary nerve injury (deltoid weakness, loss of sensation over regimental badge area) and axillary artery damage.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.question_text: Fallot's tetralogy: component that determines severity?
questions.explanation: TOF severity depends on RVOT (right ventricular outflow tract) obstruction degree. More obstruction → more R-to-L shunting → more cyanosis. Tet spells treated with squatting, knee-chest position.

questions.subject: PSM
questions.question_text: Type II error (β error) is?

options.B: Accepting false null hypothesis (missing a true effect)

questions.explanation: Type II (β) error: failing to reject a false null hypothesis = missed effect (false negative). Power = 1-β. Increased by small sample size, low effect size, high variability.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.question_text: Heinz bodies are seen in?
questions.explanation: Heinz bodies: denatured precipitated hemoglobin in G6PD deficiency (oxidative hemolysis). Seen on crystal violet stain, not Romanowsky stains.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA): characteristic finding?
questions.explanation: ABPA: central (proximal) bronchiectasis, elevated total IgE >1000 IU/mL, Aspergillus-specific IgE/IgG, eosinophilia. Rosenberg criteria.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: A 60-year-old man presents with palpitations. ECG shows irregularly irregular rhythm with no P waves. Most appropriate initial management?
questions.explanation: Atrial fibrillation: rate control is first-line unless hemodynamically unstable. Beta-blockers (metoprolol) or calcium channel blockers are used.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: A 70-year-old develops sudden onset left-sided weakness lasting 15 minutes. CT head normal. Next step?
questions.explanation: TIA: aspirin + clopidogrel (dual antiplatelet) for 21 days. ABCD² score guides risk. tPA is for ischemic stroke within 4.5 hours.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Which antiarrhythmic is SAFE in WPW with AF?
questions.explanation: WPW + AF: drugs blocking AV node (digoxin, verapamil, adenosine) are CONTRAINDICATED — may increase conduction through accessory pathway. Procainamide/DC cardioversion are safe.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Hepatorenal syndrome: most important differentiating feature from pre-renal AKI?
questions.explanation: HRS: renal failure in cirrhosis that does NOT improve with 1.5L albumin challenge. Urine Na <10 mEq/L, no proteinuria, no obstruction.

questions.subject: ENT
questions.question_text: Presbycusis: audiogram shows?
questions.explanation: Presbycusis (age-related hearing loss): bilateral symmetric high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss (cochlear hair cell degeneration). Most common cause of SNHL in elderly.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Drug of choice for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP)?
questions.explanation: PCP treatment: high-dose TMP-SMX (cotrimoxazole) x21 days. Add prednisolone if PaO2 <70 mmHg. LDH elevated, silver stain/immunofluorescence diagnostic.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question_text: Dead space in lungs: anatomical dead space is approximately?
questions.explanation: Anatomical dead space ≈ 150 mL (conducting airways). Physiological dead space = anatomical + alveolar dead space. Tidal volume ≈ 500 mL. Alveolar ventilation = (TV - dead space) × RR.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Best investigation for diagnosing DVT?
questions.explanation: Doppler ultrasound (compression US) is the first-line investigation for DVT (non-invasive, sensitive). Gold standard: venography. D-dimer: high sensitivity but low specificity.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Graves' disease autoantibody?
questions.explanation: Graves' disease: TRAb (TSI — thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin) stimulates TSH receptor → hyperthyroidism. Also anti-TPO may be positive.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.question_text: SSRI mechanism?

options.C: Blocks both serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake

questions.explanation: SSRIs: block SERT (serotonin transporter) → increased synaptic serotonin. First-line for depression, OCD, PTSD, panic disorder, social anxiety. Side effects: GI upset, sexual dysfunction, serotonin syndrome.

questions.subject: PSM
questions.question_text: Total fertility rate (TFR) is?

options.B: Average children a woman would have over her lifetime

questions.explanation: TFR: hypothetical number of children a woman would have if she lived through all reproductive years with age-specific fertility rates. Replacement level = 2.1. India ~2.0 (2023).

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question_text: During phase 2 (plateau) of ventricular action potential, main current is?

options.B: Slow Ca2+ influx and K+ efflux (balanced)

questions.explanation: Phase 2 (plateau): slow Ca2+ influx (L-type Ca channels) balanced by K+ efflux → relatively flat. This phase is unique to cardiac muscle, allows sustained contraction and prevents tetanus.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.question_text: Apgar score: what is assessed?
questions.explanation: Apgar: A=Appearance (color), P=Pulse (HR), G=Grimace (reflex irritability), A=Activity (tone), R=Respiration. Scored 0-2 each at 1 and 5 minutes. 7-10=normal, 4-6=moderate depression, <4=severe.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question_text: Cerebellum lesion: ipsilateral or contralateral signs?
questions.explanation: Cerebellar lesion: IPSILATERAL signs (cerebellum does not decussate). Features: DASHING — Dysdiadochokinesia, Ataxia (gait), Scanning speech, Hypotonia, Intention tremor, Nystagmus, Gait (wide-based).

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) persists >6 months indicates?
questions.explanation: HBsAg >6 months = chronic HBV infection. HBsAb = immunity (post-infection or vaccine). HBcAb IgM = acute infection.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question_text: Inulin clearance measures?
questions.explanation: Inulin: freely filtered, not secreted or reabsorbed → clearance = GFR (gold standard). Clinical GFR: creatinine clearance (overestimates slightly due to tubular secretion). Normal GFR: 125 mL/min.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Cowdry type A inclusion bodies are seen in?
questions.explanation: HSV encephalitis: Cowdry type A inclusions in neurons/oligodendrocytes. CMV: 'owl eye' inclusions. Rabies: Negri bodies. JC: Cowdry B.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: ADA 2023 diagnostic criteria for diabetes: fasting plasma glucose?
questions.explanation: Diabetes: FPG ≥7.0 mmol/L (126 mg/dL), 2h OGTT ≥11.1 mmol/L, HbA1c ≥6.5%, or random glucose ≥11.1 with symptoms.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.question_text: Takayasu arteritis primarily affects?
questions.explanation: Takayasu: 'pulseless disease' in young Asian women. Granulomatous inflammation of aorta/branches. ESR elevated. Complications: HTN, visual loss, claudication.

questions.subject: PSM
questions.question_text: Sensitivity is?
questions.explanation: Sensitivity = TP/(TP+FN) = ability to detect disease (true positive rate). Specificity = TN/(TN+FP). High sensitivity → good screening test. High specificity → good confirmation test.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.question_text: Multiple myeloma: characteristic finding on protein electrophoresis?
questions.explanation: Multiple myeloma: M-protein (IgG most common, then IgA) on SPEP. Bence-Jones proteins in urine. CRAB criteria: hyperCalcemia, Renal failure, Anemia, Bone lesions.

questions.subject: PSM
questions.question_text: p-value of 0.03 means?

options.A: 3% chance the alternative hypothesis is true
options.B: 3% probability of observed results if null hypothesis were true

questions.explanation: p-value: probability of obtaining results at least as extreme as observed IF null hypothesis were true. p<0.05 = statistically significant (reject null). Does NOT measure effect size.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Most common complication of TURP?
questions.explanation: Retrograde ejaculation occurs in ~90% after TURP (damage to internal urethral sphincter). TURP syndrome (hyponatremia) is another complication.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question_text: Meckel's diverticulum: remnant of?
questions.explanation: Meckel's: persistent vitelline duct. Urachus remnant: urachal cyst/sinus/fistula. Allantois → median umbilical ligament. Umbilical vein → ligamentum teres.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Churg-Strauss syndrome (EGPA) is associated with?
questions.explanation: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Churg-Strauss): p-ANCA (anti-MPO) positive. Triad: asthma, eosinophilia, vasculitis.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Stanford type A aortic dissection involves?

options.B: Ascending aorta (any dissection with ascending involvement)

questions.explanation: Stanford A: involves ascending aorta (any type) → surgical emergency. Stanford B: only descending aorta → medical management (beta-blockers).

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.question_text: Typical CDH (congenital diaphragmatic hernia) presentation at birth?

options.B: Scaphoid abdomen, respiratory distress, bowel sounds in chest
options.D: Distended abdomen, mediastinal shift away from hernia

questions.explanation: CDH: scaphoid abdomen (bowel herniated into chest), respiratory distress at birth. CXR: bowel in chest, mediastinal shift to OPPOSITE side. Bochdalek hernia: posterolateral, mostly left (85%).

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Brown-Séquard syndrome: ipsilateral findings include?
questions.explanation: Brown-Séquard (hemisection): IPSILATERAL — UMN weakness + loss of proprioception/vibration. CONTRALATERAL — loss of pain/temperature 2-3 levels below.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.question_text: ACE inhibitor that causes cough due to?
questions.explanation: ACE inhibitors: bradykinin accumulation (ACE also degrades bradykinin) → prostaglandin-mediated cough. Incidence ~15-20%. Switch to ARB (no effect on bradykinin).

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Tension pneumothorax: immediate management?
questions.explanation: Tension pneumothorax: clinical diagnosis (tracheal deviation, absent breath sounds, hypotension, JVP raised). Immediate needle decompression — do NOT wait for CXR.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.question_text: Cryptococcus neoformans: microscopy finding in CSF?
questions.explanation: Cryptococcus: polysaccharide capsule seen as clear halo on India ink. India ink and latex agglutination (capsular Ag) for diagnosis. Pigeon droppings association. DOC: amphotericin B + flucytosine.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.question_text: Psammoma bodies are seen in all EXCEPT?
questions.explanation: Psammoma bodies: concentric calcified lamellations. Seen in papillary thyroid Ca, meningioma, serous ovarian Ca, papillary renal Ca. NOT mucinous tumors.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.question_text: PET scan uses which radiotracer most commonly?
questions.explanation: 18F-FDG PET: glucose analog taken up by metabolically active cells (tumors). Whole-body staging, treatment response. Brain: Alzheimer's (hypometabolism temporal/parietal). Heart: viability (FDG = hibernating myocardium).

questions.subject: OBGYN
questions.question_text: Crown-rump length (CRL) is most accurate for gestational age in?
questions.explanation: CRL in 1st trimester (up to 14 weeks) is most accurate for gestational age (±5 days). After 14 weeks: BPD, HC, AC, FL used. 3rd trimester: least accurate (±3 weeks).

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.question_text: DOC for leprosy (paucibacillary)?
questions.explanation: PB leprosy (1-5 patches): Rifampicin monthly + Dapsone daily for 6 months. MB leprosy (>5 patches or smear positive): MDT x 12 months. WHO regimen.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.question_text: Botulinum toxin mechanism?

options.B: Prevents ACh release by cleaving SNARE proteins

questions.explanation: Botulinum toxin: cleaves SNARE proteins (SNAP-25, synaptobrevin) → prevents ACh vesicle fusion → flaccid paralysis. Used for dystonia, cosmetics, achalasia.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Most common cause of sudden cardiac death in young athletes?
questions.explanation: HOCM (HCM) is the most common cause of sudden death in young athletes in the USA. Pathognomonic: asymmetric septal hypertrophy.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.question_text: Volume of distribution >1 L/kg suggests?
questions.explanation: High Vd: drug is extensively distributed to tissues (e.g., amiodarone Vd >60 L/kg). Low Vd (<0.1 L/kg): drug confined to plasma (heparin, warfarin).

questions.subject: Ophthalmology
questions.question_text: Retinoblastoma: inheritance?
questions.explanation: Retinoblastoma: RB1 gene (tumor suppressor, chromosome 13q14). Knudson's 2-hit hypothesis. Hereditary: AD, bilateral, younger. Sporadic: unilateral, older. Leukocoria + strabismus.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Most common cause of death in SLE?
questions.explanation: Modern SLE: cardiovascular disease (accelerated atherosclerosis) is now the leading cause of death. Historically renal failure was first.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.question_text: Schneider's first-rank symptoms of schizophrenia include all EXCEPT?
questions.explanation: Schneider's first-rank symptoms: thought insertion/withdrawal/broadcasting, made feelings/impulses/acts, somatic passivity, auditory (running commentary, third person, echo of thought). Visual hallucinations are NOT FRS.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: A patient with trigeminal neuralgia: electric shock-like pain in V2/V3 territory. Drug of choice?
questions.explanation: Carbamazepine (tegretol) is DOC for trigeminal neuralgia. Blocks sodium channels. If refractory: MVD (microvascular decompression).

questions.subject: OBGYN
questions.question_text: Triple test in 2nd trimester for Down syndrome shows?
questions.explanation: Down syndrome (T21) triple test: ↓AFP, ↑hCG, ↓unconjugated estriol (uE3). Quadruple test adds inhibin A (↑). Neural tube defects: ↑AFP.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.question_text: Fixed drug eruption (FDE): characteristic feature?

options.A: Occurs in different sites each time
options.B: Recurs at same site on re-exposure to drug

questions.explanation: FDE: oval/round well-demarcated erythematous plaque at SAME site on re-exposure. Residual hyperpigmentation. Common drugs: cotrimoxazole, NSAIDs, metronidazole, tetracycline.

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.question_text: Ketamine mechanism and unique property?

options.B: NMDA antagonist — dissociative anesthesia, bronchodilation, preserves airway reflexes

questions.explanation: Ketamine: NMDA receptor antagonist → dissociative anesthesia. Unique: maintains airway reflexes, causes bronchodilation (good in asthma/status asthmaticus), increases HR/BP. Causes emergence hallucinations.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.question_text: Birth weight of 1000g is classified as?
questions.explanation: Birth weight categories: LBW <2500g, VLBW <1500g, ELBW <1000g. Small for gestational age (SGA) <10th percentile for GA. AGA: 10th-90th percentile.

questions.subject: OBGYN
questions.question_text: Polyhydramnios is associated with?
questions.explanation: Polyhydramnios (AFI >25): impaired fetal swallowing (anencephaly, esophageal/duodenal atresia) or increased production. Oligohydramnios: decreased fetal urine output (renal agenesis = Potter sequence).

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.question_text: HIDA (hepatobiliary iminodiacetic acid) scan is used for?
questions.explanation: HIDA scan: assesses biliary function and gallbladder ejection fraction. Used for: acute cholecystitis (no filling of GB), sphincter of Oddi dysfunction, biliary atresia. Normal GBEF >35%.

questions.subject: Forensic Medicine
questions.question_text: Carbon monoxide poisoning: cherry-red color of skin is due to?
questions.explanation: CO poisoning: HbCO (cherry-pink/red discoloration of mucous membranes, lividity, organs). CO has 240x affinity for Hb vs O2. Treatment: 100% O2 (hyperbaric in severe). CO also binds cytochrome oxidase.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: A child has butterfly rash, arthritis, and renal involvement. ANA positive. Best confirmatory test?
questions.explanation: Anti-dsDNA confirms SLE and correlates with disease activity/nephritis. Anti-Smith is most specific but anti-dsDNA is used for monitoring.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Nelson's syndrome occurs after?
questions.explanation: Nelson's syndrome: bilateral adrenalectomy for Cushing's disease → loss of cortisol feedback → rapid ACTH-secreting pituitary tumor growth + hyperpigmentation.

questions.subject: OBGYN
questions.question_text: Ectopic pregnancy: most common site?
questions.explanation: Ectopic pregnancy: 95% in fallopian tube. Most common site: AMPULLA (70%). Then isthmus (12%). Cornual/interstitial: most dangerous (ruptures late, more hemorrhage).

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: A patient presents with chest pain. ECG shows ST elevation in II, III, aVF. Artery involved?
questions.explanation: Inferior MI (II, III, aVF) = RCA territory (85% cases). Check RV leads (V3R, V4R) for right ventricular MI.

questions.subject: PSM
questions.question_text: Ecological fallacy is a risk in?
questions.explanation: Ecological fallacy: association found at group level may not apply to individuals. E.g., countries with high fat intake have high heart disease rates — doesn't mean each individual with high fat intake gets heart disease.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Most common post-operative complication in first 24 hours?
questions.explanation: Reactionary hemorrhage: within 24 hours, due to dislodged clot or missed vessel. Secondary hemorrhage: 7-14 days, due to infection.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.question_text: Acanthosis nigricans is associated with?
questions.explanation: Acanthosis nigricans: velvety hyperpigmented thickening at neck, axillae, groins. Associated with insulin resistance (most common), DM2, obesity, PCOS. Malignant AN: associated with gastric Ca.

questions.subject: PSM
questions.question_text: Gold standard study for causation?
questions.explanation: RCT is the gold standard for establishing causation (randomization removes confounding). For observational evidence: meta-analysis > cohort > case-control > cross-sectional.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Fontaine classification stage IIb?
questions.explanation: Fontaine: I=asymptomatic, IIa=claudication >200m, IIb=claudication <200m, III=rest pain, IV=ulceration/gangrene.

questions.subject: OBGYN
questions.question_text: CA-125 is elevated in?
questions.explanation: CA-125: marker for serous epithelial ovarian Ca. Also elevated in endometriosis, PID, menstruation (non-specific). Used for monitoring, not screening.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Pannus formation is a feature of?
questions.explanation: Pannus = granulation tissue in RA that erodes cartilage and bone. Anti-CCP (anti-citrullinated protein antibody) is most specific for RA.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Dressler's syndrome occurs?
questions.explanation: Dressler's (post-cardiac injury) syndrome: autoimmune pericarditis 2-10 weeks post-MI or cardiac surgery. Fever, pleuritis, pericardial effusion.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Wilson's disease: gene mutated?
questions.explanation: Wilson's disease: ATP7B mutation (chromosome 13) → copper accumulation. Features: Kayser-Fleischer rings, liver disease, neuropsychiatric symptoms.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: CEAP classification is used for?
questions.explanation: CEAP: Clinical-Etiology-Anatomy-Pathophysiology classification for chronic venous disorders. C0=no signs to C6=active ulcer.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: CURB-65 score of 3 in community-acquired pneumonia indicates?
questions.explanation: CURB-65: Confusion, Urea>7, RR≥30, BP<90/60, age≥65. Score 0-1: home; 2: hospital; 3-5: hospital/ICU. Score 3 = hospitalization.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Drug of choice for status epilepticus?
questions.explanation: Status epilepticus: benzodiazepines first (lorazepam IV or diazepam). If persistent: levetiracetam/valproate/phenytoin. Propofol for refractory.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.question_text: Aminoglycosides should be avoided in renal failure because?
questions.explanation: Aminoglycosides (gentamicin, amikacin): nephrotoxic (proximal tubule) + ototoxic (vestibular/cochlear). Requires dose adjustment in renal failure. Monitor TDM.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question_text: Rate-limiting enzyme of glycolysis?
questions.explanation: PFK-1 is the key regulatory enzyme of glycolysis. Inhibited by: ATP, citrate. Activated by: AMP, ADP, fructose-2,6-bisphosphate (most potent activator). Site of glycolytic control.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Gitelman syndrome vs Bartter syndrome: differentiating feature?

options.A: Gitelman has hypocalciuria, Bartter has hypercalciuria

questions.explanation: Gitelman: NCCT mutation, hypocalciuria, hypomagnesemia, presents in adults. Bartter: NKCC2/ROMK/CIC-Kb, hypercalciuria, presents in infancy.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: In Brugada syndrome, characteristic ECG change is seen in?
questions.explanation: Brugada: coved-type ST elevation in V1-V2 (Type 1 pattern). Causes sudden death due to VF. SCN5A mutation.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.question_text: Hydralazine mechanism?
questions.explanation: Hydralazine: direct arteriolar smooth muscle relaxation → decreased SVR → reflex tachycardia. Used in hypertensive emergency in pregnancy (with methyldopa).

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: ECG shows peaked T waves and widened QRS. Most likely electrolyte?
questions.explanation: Hyperkalemia sequence: peaked T → flat P → wide QRS → sine wave → VF. Treatment: calcium gluconate first (membrane stabilization).

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.question_text: Leishmania: vector and site in macrophage?
questions.explanation: Leishmania: sandfly (Phlebotomus in old world, Lutzomyia in new world). Amastigotes in macrophage phagolysosomes. DOC: liposomal amphotericin B (India) or miltefosine.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.question_text: Keloid vs hypertrophic scar: differentiating feature?
questions.explanation: Keloid: extends BEYOND wound margins, does not regress spontaneously, type III > type I collagen, more common in dark skin. Hypertrophic: within margins, may regress.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: CSF in bacterial meningitis shows?
questions.explanation: Bacterial meningitis: low glucose (<45 mg/dL), high protein, neutrophilic pleocytosis. Viral: normal/high glucose, moderate protein, lymphocytes.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Non-falciparum malaria with longest incubation period?
questions.explanation: P. malariae: quartan malaria, incubation 18-40 days. Causes nephrotic syndrome. No hypnozoites. P. vivax/ovale: relapse from hypnozoites, treat with primaquine.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: CREST syndrome includes all EXCEPT?
questions.explanation: CREST = Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia. Raynaud's IS included — the trick is if Renal is listed (not part of CREST). All 5 are present.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question_text: Scurvy: pathophysiology?

options.B: Vitamin C deficiency → impaired collagen synthesis

questions.explanation: Scurvy: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) deficiency → impaired hydroxylation of proline/lysine → abnormal collagen → perifollicular hemorrhage, corkscrew hair, bleeding gums, poor wound healing.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Achalasia cardia: manometric finding?
questions.explanation: Achalasia: failure of LES relaxation (high resting pressure) + aperistalsis of esophageal body. Bird-beak appearance on barium swallow.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Charcot's triad in cholangitis?
questions.explanation: Charcot's triad: fever+rigor + RUQ pain + jaundice. Reynolds pentad adds shock + confusion (severe cholangitis). Treatment: ERCP + antibiotics.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.question_text: Drug of choice for absence seizures?
questions.explanation: Absence seizures: ethosuximide (DOC, pure absence only) or valproate (especially if mixed seizures). Carbamazepine/phenytoin can WORSEN absence seizures.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Ideal suture material for abdominal wall closure?
questions.explanation: Mass closure with loop PDS (slowly absorbable) is ideal for abdominal wall. Provides prolonged tensile strength (>6 months) needed for healing.

questions.subject: Orthopedics
questions.question_text: Colles' fracture: classical deformity?

options.A: Dinner fork deformity (dorsal displacement of distal fragment)

questions.explanation: Colles' fracture: distal radius fracture with dorsal displacement and radial deviation → dinner fork deformity. Smith's fracture (reverse Colles'): volar displacement → garden spade deformity.

questions.subject: Radiology
questions.question_text: Tc-99m sestamibi scan is used for?
questions.explanation: Tc-99m sestamibi (MIBI): myocardial perfusion imaging — localizes viable myocardium. Also used for parathyroid adenoma localization. Tc-99m pertechnetate: thyroid scan.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Resting tremor, cogwheel rigidity, bradykinesia, postural instability — diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Parkinson's disease: TRAP (Tremor-Rigidity-Akinesia-Postural instability). Loss of dopaminergic neurons in substantia nigra. Lewy bodies.

questions.subject: Orthopedics
questions.question_text: Most common bone tumor (primary malignant)?
questions.explanation: Osteosarcoma: most common primary malignant bone tumor (excluding hematological). Metaphysis of distal femur/proximal tibia. Codman's triangle + sunray spiculation on X-ray.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.question_text: Granulomatous inflammation is caused by all EXCEPT?
questions.explanation: Non-caseating granulomas: sarcoidosis, Crohn's, foreign body, berylliosis. Caseating: TB, histoplasma, leprosy. Acute appendicitis = acute suppurative inflammation.

questions.subject: OBGYN
questions.question_text: Normal fetal heart rate range?
questions.explanation: Normal FHR: 110-160 bpm. Tachycardia >160, bradycardia <110. Baseline variability 6-25 bpm = normal. Loss of variability + late decelerations = fetal distress.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Which antibody in Sjogren's syndrome is associated with neonatal lupus and heart block?
questions.explanation: Anti-Ro/SSA crosses placenta causing neonatal lupus (rash, cytopenias, complete heart block). Anti-La/SSB less commonly associated.

questions.subject: Psychiatry
questions.question_text: Lithium: indication and monitoring?

options.B: Bipolar disorder; monitor serum lithium, TFT, renal function, ECG

questions.explanation: Lithium: mood stabilizer for bipolar disorder (acute mania + prophylaxis). Narrow therapeutic window (0.6-1.2 mEq/L). Monitor: lithium level, TFT (hypothyroidism), renal function (nephrogenic DI), ECG.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.question_text: Coagulative necrosis is seen in all EXCEPT?
questions.explanation: Brain infarction → LIQUEFACTIVE necrosis (rich in hydrolytic enzymes and fat). All other solid organs: coagulative necrosis (cell architecture preserved).

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question_text: Functional residual capacity (FRC) cannot be measured by spirometry because?

options.B: FRC includes residual volume which cannot be exhaled

questions.explanation: FRC = ERV + RV. RV (residual volume) cannot be exhaled → not measurable by spirometry. Measured by: helium dilution, nitrogen washout, or body plethysmography.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.question_text: Mechanism of fluoroquinolone resistance?
questions.explanation: Fluoroquinolone resistance: primarily mutations in gyrA (DNA gyrase subunit A) or parC (topoisomerase IV). Also: efflux pumps, porin changes.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question_text: Diaphragm opening for IVC?
questions.explanation: Diaphragm apertures: IVC = T8 (caval opening in central tendon), Esophagus = T10 (esophageal hiatus — vagus, esophageal branches of left gastric), Aorta = T12 (aortic hiatus — thoracic duct, azygos).

questions.subject: Anaesthesia
questions.question_text: ASA physical status grade IV?

options.D: Severe systemic disease, constant threat to life

questions.explanation: ASA classification: I=healthy, II=mild disease (well-controlled DM/HTN), III=severe disease (uncontrolled DM, COPD), IV=constant threat to life (recent MI, severe CHF), V=moribund, VI=brain-dead for organ donation.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Glasgow Coma Scale: best score for E4V5M6?
questions.explanation: GCS = E+V+M = 4+5+6 = 15 (normal). Eyes 1-4, Verbal 1-5, Motor 1-6. GCS ≤8 = intubate.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Liddle syndrome is characterized by?
questions.explanation: Liddle syndrome: gain-of-function ENaC mutation → Na retention → hypertension, hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, LOW aldosterone/renin.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.question_text: Caput succedaneum vs cephalhematoma: correct statement?

options.B: Caput crosses suture lines, cephalhematoma does not

questions.explanation: Caput succedaneum: edema of scalp, crosses sutures, present at birth, resolves in days. Cephalhematoma: subperiosteal hemorrhage, does NOT cross sutures, appears hours after birth, resolves weeks-months.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.question_text: Competitive antagonist effect on dose-response curve?

options.A: Shifts left, no change in Emax
options.B: Shifts right, no change in Emax

questions.explanation: Competitive antagonist: shifts DRC to RIGHT (increased EC50/reduced potency) but Emax UNCHANGED (can be overcome by increasing agonist dose). Irreversible: reduces Emax.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Hartmann's solution is another name for?
questions.explanation: Ringer's lactate = Hartmann's solution. Contains Na, K, Ca, Cl, lactate. Near-physiological, preferred for trauma/surgery over NS (less hyperchloremic acidosis).

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.question_text: Barrett's esophagus: type of metaplasia?
questions.explanation: Barrett's: normal squamous epithelium → specialized intestinal metaplasia (columnar with goblet cells). Risk of adenocarcinoma. PPI reduces progression.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.question_text: Diphtheria toxin inhibits protein synthesis by?
questions.explanation: Diphtheria toxin: ADP-ribosylates EF-2 (elongation factor 2) → halts translocation → protein synthesis inhibition. Similar to Pseudomonas exotoxin A.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Ankle-brachial index (ABI) <0.4 indicates?
questions.explanation: ABI: >1.0 normal, 0.7-0.9 mild, 0.4-0.7 moderate, <0.4 critical limb ischemia (rest pain/gangrene). >1.3 suggests calcification.

questions.subject: OBGYN
questions.question_text: Asherman's syndrome is?
questions.explanation: Asherman's syndrome: intrauterine adhesions (synechiae) after D&C/infection → amenorrhea, infertility. Diagnosis: hysteroscopy. Treatment: hysteroscopic adhesiolysis + estrogen.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.question_text: Philadelphia chromosome is seen in?
questions.explanation: Philadelphia chromosome: t(9;22) BCR-ABL1 fusion. Classic in CML but also in 20-30% adult ALL. Treated with imatinib (TKI).

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question_text: Upper motor neuron lesion signs include?
questions.explanation: UMN lesion: spastic paralysis, increased tone, hyperreflexia, Babinski positive (extensor plantar), no atrophy. LMN lesion: flaccid, hypotonia, hyporeflexia, wasting, fasciculations.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.question_text: Alpha-2 agonist used as antihypertensive (central action)?
questions.explanation: Clonidine: alpha-2 agonist acting centrally (locus coeruleus) → reduces sympathetic outflow → lowers BP and HR. Also used for opioid withdrawal, ADHD.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.question_text: Virus causing subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE)?
questions.explanation: SSPE: defective measles virus persists in CNS after years → progressive dementia, myoclonus, EEG burst suppression. High CSF measles antibody titer is diagnostic.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: CD4 count at which PCP prophylaxis with cotrimoxazole is started in HIV?
questions.explanation: PCP (Pneumocystis jirovecii) prophylaxis: cotrimoxazole when CD4 <200. MAC prophylaxis: azithromycin when CD4 <50.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: A patient has wide-complex tachycardia at 180 bpm. Best initial step?
questions.explanation: Stable wide-complex tachycardia (likely VT): amiodarone is first-line. Verapamil is CONTRAINDICATED in VT.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question_text: Recurrent laryngeal nerve: surgical danger in?
questions.explanation: RLN runs in tracheoesophageal groove. At highest risk during total thyroidectomy. Right RLN loops around subclavian artery; Left loops around arch of aorta (longer, more vulnerable in mediastinal surgery).

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.question_text: Auer rods are found in?
questions.explanation: Auer rods: pink/purple needle-like inclusions in blasts (myeloperoxidase-positive azurophilic granules). Pathognomonic of AML. APML (M3) has many Auer rods (faggot cells).

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.question_text: Lowenstein-Jensen medium is used for?
questions.explanation: LJ medium: enriched egg-based medium for TB culture. Growth in 3-8 weeks. BacTec/MGIT: rapid liquid culture for TB (14 days).

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Most common cause of Cushing's syndrome?
questions.explanation: Most common overall cause of Cushing's: EXOGENOUS steroids. Among endogenous: Cushing's disease (pituitary ACTH) is most common.

questions.subject: Ophthalmology
questions.question_text: Normal intraocular pressure range?
questions.explanation: Normal IOP: 10-21 mmHg (Goldmann applanation tonometry is gold standard). Ocular hypertension: IOP >21 without glaucomatous damage. Primary open-angle glaucoma: often IOP >21.

questions.subject: Orthopedics
questions.question_text: Cobb's angle is used to measure?
questions.explanation: Cobb's angle: measures scoliosis on standing AP X-ray. Angle between superior endplate of upper end vertebra and inferior endplate of lower end vertebra. <10°: normal variation; >10°: scoliosis.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.question_text: Ring forms and banana-shaped gametocytes are features of?
questions.explanation: P. falciparum: ring forms (multiple rings/cell, accole forms), banana/crescent-shaped gametocytes. Maurer's clefts. Causes cerebral malaria, severe anemia, blackwater fever.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Cushing's ulcer is associated with?
questions.explanation: Cushing's ulcer: stress ulcer from raised ICP/head injury (vagal stimulation → acid hypersecretion). Curling's ulcer: burns. Both prevented with PPI.

questions.subject: ENT
questions.question_text: Saddle nose deformity is caused by?

options.B: Destruction of nasal septal cartilage (syphilis, Wegener's, relapsing polychondritis, trauma)

questions.explanation: Saddle nose: collapse of dorsum from cartilage/bone destruction. Causes: tertiary syphilis (classic), Wegener's GPA, relapsing polychondritis, trauma, cocaine abuse.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.question_text: Gonorrhea: site of chromosomal resistance mechanism?
questions.explanation: N. gonorrhoeae resistance: chromosomally-mediated reduced susceptibility (altered PBP + efflux + porin) or plasmid-mediated (beta-lactamase = PPNG). Ceftriaxone is current DOC.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Sentinel pile is associated with?
questions.explanation: Sentinel pile: skin tag at lower end of chronic anal fissure (at 6 o'clock position posteriorly). Treated with lateral internal sphincterotomy.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Drug that prolongs QT interval and is associated with torsades de pointes?
questions.explanation: Amiodarone prolongs QT but paradoxically rarely causes TdP. However, it is listed as a QT-prolonging drug. Other drugs: quinidine, sotalol, haloperidol, macrolides.

questions.subject: Physiology
questions.question_text: Oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve: Bohr effect is a shift due to?
questions.explanation: Bohr effect: increased CO2/decreased pH shifts ODC RIGHT → lower Hb affinity for O2 → more O2 released to tissues. Exercise: right shift. Altitude/alkalosis: left shift. 2,3-DPG also shifts right.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.question_text: Normal PDA closure: timing?
questions.explanation: PDA: functional closure in 24-72h (prostaglandin levels fall, O2 tension rises). Anatomical closure: 2-3 weeks. Preterm infants: indomethacin/ibuprofen to close PDA. If persistent: surgical ligation.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Most common position of Meckel's diverticulum?
questions.explanation: Meckel's: rule of 2s — 2% population, 2 feet from ileocecal valve, 2 inches long, 2x common in males, by age 2, 2 types of ectopic mucosa (gastric/pancreatic). ANTIMESENTERIC border.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.question_text: Auspitz's sign is seen in?
questions.explanation: Auspitz sign: pinpoint bleeding on removing psoriatic scale (thinned suprapapillary epidermis). Other psoriasis signs: Koebner, candle grease, Woronoff's ring. Nail: pitting (most common), oil drop.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question_text: Enzyme deficient in G6PD deficiency?
questions.explanation: G6PD deficiency: X-linked. G6PD generates NADPH via pentose phosphate pathway → maintains GSH → protects RBCs from oxidative stress. Trigger: infections, drugs (primaquine, dapsone).

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.question_text: Digoxin toxicity: most common cardiac arrhythmia?
questions.explanation: Digoxin toxicity: most common arrhythmia = PVCs (especially bigeminy). Also causes: paroxysmal atrial tachycardia with block (PAT with block) — hallmark. Treatment: digoxin-specific Fab.

questions.subject: Biochemistry
questions.question_text: Pellagra is deficiency of?
questions.explanation: Pellagra: niacin (B3) deficiency. 3 D's: Dermatitis, Diarrhea, Dementia. Casal's necklace (photosensitive skin around neck). Also in isoniazid use (depletes pyridoxine needed for niacin synthesis).

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Osborne (J) waves on ECG are seen in?
questions.explanation: Osborne/J waves: positive deflection at J-point, pathognomonic of hypothermia. Also seen in hypercalcemia but hypothermia is classic.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Aschoff bodies are found in?
questions.explanation: Aschoff bodies (granulomas with Anitschkow cells/caterpillar cells) are pathognomonic of rheumatic fever, seen in myocardium.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Craniopharyngioma: most common presentation in children?
questions.explanation: Craniopharyngioma: bitemporal hemianopia (chiasmal compression), growth failure (GH deficiency), DI. Calcification on imaging is classic.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Modified Wells score is used for?
questions.explanation: Modified Wells score: pre-test probability of DVT. Score ≥2 = likely DVT → ultrasound. Score <2 = unlikely → D-dimer first.

questions.subject: Orthopedics
questions.question_text: Paget's disease: lab findings?

options.A: Elevated ALP, normal Ca and PO4
options.B: Elevated Ca, low PO4, elevated ALP

questions.explanation: Paget's disease (osteitis deformans): markedly elevated ALP (bone-specific), NORMAL Ca and PO4. Increased bone turnover. Complications: hearing loss, heart failure, sarcomatous transformation (1%).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question_text: Muscles of mastication: all EXCEPT?
questions.explanation: Muscles of mastication (CN V3): masseter, temporalis, medial/lateral pterygoid. Buccinator is a muscle of facial expression (CN VII). Buccinator aids chewing but not a muscle of mastication.

questions.subject: OBGYN
questions.question_text: Most common ovarian tumor in young women?
questions.explanation: Dermoid cyst (mature cystic teratoma): most common benign ovarian tumor in reproductive age. Contains ectodermal elements (hair, teeth, sebum). Rokitansky protuberance.

questions.subject: PSM
questions.question_text: Berkson's bias is seen in?
questions.explanation: Berkson's bias: selection bias in hospital-based case-control studies — hospitalized controls may not represent general population (over-represent sick people). Also called hospital admission rate bias.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.question_text: Urinary stone most radiolucent on plain X-ray?
questions.explanation: Uric acid stones: radiolucent (not visible on plain X-ray), visible on CT/ultrasound. Calcium stones: most radiopaque. Cystine: faintly opaque.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.question_text: Celiac disease antibody for diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Anti-tTG IgA (tissue transglutaminase) is most sensitive/specific for celiac disease. Confirm with duodenal biopsy (villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, intraepithelial lymphocytes).

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.question_text: Gram-positive organism that does NOT decolorize with acid?
questions.explanation: Mycobacterium: 'acid-fast' — resists decolorization with acid-alcohol in Ziehl-Neelsen stain due to mycolic acid in cell wall. Appears red (carbol fuchsin).

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.question_text: Amiodarone: longest half-life?
questions.explanation: Amiodarone: half-life 40-55 days (average 50 days). Contains iodine, causes thyroid dysfunction, pulmonary fibrosis, corneal deposits, photosensitivity. Class III antiarrhythmic.
